full_judgment:
2. Facts are simple:-Plaintiff is the appellant.  She filed the suit being Title Suit No. 554 of 1978 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Dhaka against the defendants for ejectment from the suit shop on the ground of being defaulter and for her own bonafide requirement. The suit was contested and the trial Court decreed the suit and found the defendants as defaulter and also for subletting the premises in breach of agreement. Defendants filed appeal being Title Appeal No. 327 of 1984 and the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka dismissed the appeal upon a finding that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were defaulters and defendant No. 3 was sub-lessee. 

 "Because in view of the provisions of section 18(3) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance and in view of the admitted facts and the materials on record that the defendant No.3 who was taken in as a partner in the business by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 under a duly registered deed of partnership, became a tenant under the plaintiff by operation of law and no decree for eviction can legally be passed against him." 

 "(3) Where any tenant has sublet any premises or part thereof with the consent of the landlord or in accordance with the terms of the contract with the landlord expressly permitting subletting, or where any tenant has sublet any premises or part thereof used or mainly used by him for commercial or industrial purposes and has also transferred such commercial or industrial undertaking together with such premises or part, the person to whom such premises or part have or has been so sublet shall, on the lawful  determination of the interest of the tenant in  such premises or part otherwise than by virtue of a decree or order obtained by the landlord on any of the grounds specified in clause(e) of the proviso to sub-section (1), be deemed to be a  tenant in respect of such premises or part, as the case may be, holding directly under the landlord on the terms and conditions on which such person would have held under the tenant if the interest of the tenant has not been so determined." 

 11. Mr. Bhuiyan argued that on their own showing defendants had sub-let the premises and they were also defaulters. Two Courts have found them defaulters and the suit was decreed accordingly. Only in the High Court Division the point was taken that even if they were defaulters they were not liable to be ejected because defendant No. 3 is a partner of defendant Nos. 1 and 2. Mr. Bhuiyan argued that in the tenancy agreement only defendant Nos. 1 and 2 were parties and no agreement was concluded with defendant No. 3. On their own showing defendant No. 3 joined later in the firm as partner but without any consent of the landlord. So it is contended that the question of permission of the landlord could never arise. Mr. Bhuiyan next argued that if the tenants had sublet the premises which was used by them for commercial purposes which must have been transferred to the person to whom such premises have been sublet and it is only then "on the lawful determination of the interest of the tenant in such premises", he shall be deemed to be a tenant in respect of such premises holding directly under the landlord on the same terms and conditions but here, it is argued, no interest have been transferred to defendant No. 3. On the other hand, it is the case of the defendants that they have taken defendant No. 3 as partner. It is argued that partnership is one thing and transfer of interest is completely different. Hence it is submitted that section 18(3) has no application and the High Court Division was in error in coming to the conclusion. 

 (a) the person to whom such premises or part have or has been so sublet shall (i) on the lawful determination of the interest of the tenant in such premises or part otherwise than by virtue of a decree or order obtained by the landlord on any of the grounds specified in clause (e) of the proviso to sub-section (1), (ii) be deemed to be a tenant in respect of such premises or part, as the case may be, holding directly under the landlord on the terms and conditions on which such person would have held under the tenant if the interest of the tenant had not been so determined."
